_purpose: #158 triage ground truth: the human-labeled per-ADR scope verdict for every benchmark ADR, scored against the resolver's per-edge verdicts as a runtime/tooling/none confusion matrix.
_how_to_label: Read the ADR at adr_path in the repo's pinned worktree. Fill expected_scope with 'runtime', 'tooling' or 'none' (ADR 019 decision 2 vocabulary: runtime governs shipped code, tooling is the dev toolchain, none is not a dependency/implementation relation at all). Set label_source to 'human' and add a one-line notes entry when you fill one in. Gold context for each ADR (its expected constraints and a note) lives in benchmark/gold/<repo>_gold.json under the same adr_id; has-gold ADRs are the recall-safety ones. Rows whose label_source is null are unlabeled.
_anchoring_note: Deliberately NOT included: what the committed #157 fixture run produced for each ADR. Seeing the machine's verdict before labeling would anchor the ground truth (#158 axis 2 is the instrument that decides whether the triage stays).
_contested_note: Resolved 2026-09-17 on #158. flowkit ADR-0008/0009/0010 stay tooling (the #157 named list), ADR-0011/0012 stay none. Recorded caveat for 0010: tooling edges are excluded from FP accounting, so grounding the absent AutoFlow reads clean.

_rule_note: Label rule (decided 2026-09-17 on #158): expected_scope is the scope every edge of that ADR should carry, judged by the ADR's decision role (runtime | tooling | none as defined in ADR 019 decision 2); `none` means the correct observable output is zero edges. Groundability at the pin is a second, separate axis carried by the benchmark gold's 'emit no edges' notes, not by this field. Non-Python-namespace technology decisions (front-end stack, doc-site generator, Rust crate layout, QA process) are tooling. ADR 019 recall-safety rows carry `recall_safety` in addition to expected_scope.
